items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: another terrific trumpet player that I picked up in the eastern states, Billy Douglas. He... did arranging.

ctx.x: You had a regular arranger for your band?

There was five fellas in the band that arranged at one time. Harold Holmes later on when Jimmy Johnson was getting a little slow, we added Harold Holmes to the bass section. We also had a tuba, so we had a tuba, two bass fiddles in the band at the same time. Harold Holmes wrote the arrangements, another terrific trumpet player that I picked up in the eastern states, Billy Douglas. He, unfortunately he was, oh he liked to hit the bottle too much we say. But he would have been one of the mighty, mighty greats for…
But I'm just agreeing that I do some of that myself.

items.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ... Billy Douglas. [INTERVIEWEE] Well, he's still alive. I don't know the last I heard he was in the town. Oh, no. He's out now. He is in jail.

ctx.x: I just wonder, because so many people arrange at the piano and... Most of them do.

Well, we had another one like all that didn't use the piano. He might know anything about the piano. It's for Billy Douglas to sound like the whole arrangement out of his head. He couldn't touch any history. What about the... Yeah, it is.
We can continue. Did you have any trouble with transposition or anything? No. I mean for the various instruments.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: Billy Douglas and Dink Taylor, man. They would turn that shirt around. Now those two, they were characters.

ctx.x: Yeah, I see. Now did anybody, when they had a dirty shirt, would anybody ever do a thing with wearing the shirts inside and out?

Yes. Billy Douglas and Dink Taylor, man. They would turn that shirt around. Now those two, they were characters. I found this so funny. Yeah, my wife possibly told you that. Oh yes, she did. Sure she did.
Now this Judge Sondas who made the decision with Sandoz, how do you spell his name?

There wasn't any main arrangers. Harold Holmes wrote his. Billy Douglas wrote his. And Herbert Hall. If a guy would get an idea, he would write it down. But no one was, you're referring to something like in Jimmy Luster's band, where Si Oliver was the main arranger.
Well, no, there might be five main arrangers and maybe one guy would only do two.
